title: Aggregate summary of the existing held-out twin comparison
reviewStatus: Aggregate values checked against saved report JSON and evaluation source code; no participant-level results were opened and no benchmark was rerun.
interpretation: Retrospective five-hour replay with recorded future inputs. This is not a prospective forecast benchmark or validation of altered-dose counterfactuals.
sourceRepository: t1d-twin development repository; source report files are not copied into this portfolio.

protocol.forecastConditioning: Recorded future insulin, logged meals, and available recorded context; the twin warm-start also replays six hours of preceding recorded inputs and then anchors to the first CGM point.
protocol.pairwiseRmseInference: 95% interval resamples participants with replacement and carries along each selected participant's full sequence vector; the reported Wilcoxon p-value is calculated over flattened per-sequence paired differences and is not participant-clustered.
protocol.lowEventDefinition: At least three consecutive five-minute readings below 70 mg/dL during the five-hour window.
protocol.noiseMatchedBaseline: T1DSim_AI and ReplayBG point predictions receive 32 simulated noise draws per sequence using the twin-fit residual spread and a 6% proportional component.

hypoglycemia.interpretation: Seven events are insufficient for a useful hypoglycemia comparison.

replayBgComparison.reason: The available aggregate report uses twin_final.json rather than twin_v2.json.

limitations: The comparison is conditional replay: held-out future delivered insulin, logged meals, and available context are supplied from records. It is not a forecast made only from information available at the origin.
The t1d-twin warm arm uses six hours of pre-sequence input history; T1DSim_AI does not use that history. Shared windows therefore do not mean identical information sets.

The learning-rate-1e-3 T1DSim_AI run is reported as tuned, but no nested validation or selection protocol was found. Treat this comparison as exploratory because tuning may have used the same held-out windows.

The aggregate reports identify the fit by filename but do not contain model-weight hashes, raw-input hashes, dataset revision, or the exact empirical-prior fit set. Source code supports leave-one-person-out priors, but this cannot be confirmed for these specific saved fits from the aggregate report alone.
RMSE Wilcoxon p-values are sequence-level, while confidence intervals use participant-cluster bootstrap. Repeated windows within a person make the p-values potentially overconfident.
The current scoring source shadows its assimilation flag with a local list, so assimilation rows are excluded from this summary; only the warm, non-assimilated arm is reported.
The HUPA-UCM hypoglycemia result is based on 50 events; T1D-UOM has only seven. Neither supports clinical risk claims.

Counterfactual accuracy for changed insulin settings has not been established against observed treatment changes or prospective outcomes. Agreement across fitted variants is robustness evidence, not validation of alternate-dose outcomes.
The original aggregate report JSON files contain participant identifier lists and are not included here. This summary keeps only aggregate counts, metrics, and source hashes.
